thread:
Elena (AE): Heads up — Peridot POC kicked off this morning. Legal looped in but they flagged model provenance + variant guarantees. Need quick compatibility checklist before we hand to infra.
Sam R.: Quick summary of asks from their engineering: 1) support for custom llama30b quant variant, 2) KV-cache persistence across warmups, 3) latency under 120ms p50 at 4k prompt lengths.
Anya (Solutions): They also want to evaluate embedding drift on our quantized variant. Can we surface a recommended quant/profile matrix?
Marco (Infra): We ran a small perf pass on a similar model yesterday. With q4_k_mixed on A10G we hit ~95ms p50 for 2k prompts at batch=4. At 4k it climbs; need continuous batching tuned.
Sam R.: Good. Two gating items for cataloging: (A) model artifact SHA and config (hf repo + weights + tokenizer) and (B) a compatibility manifest for quantized variants (which kernels supported).
Elena (AE): Legal asked about redistribution / license flags for that custom variant. Owen — can you confirm whether we can host that variant in the catalog or if it must remain customer-only?
Owen (Security): Initial read — license looks permissive but we need a signed customer attestation if they uploaded a fork. Also need to add an entry to our security questionnaire: 'Is model an unmodified upstream release? Y/N' — if N, we escalate to Risk for IP review.
Anya (Solutions): For the evals team: recommend these prompt sets: customer-docs summarization, multi-turn chat with injected memory, and embedding similarity on 10k rows. We'll need a way to pin model version in the POC.
Marco (Infra): For pinning, we can create a catalog variant entry like: 
```
model: peridot/llama30b-custom
version: peridot-2026-03-18
quant: q4_k_mixed
kernels: [cuda_attention_v2, fused_mlp]
```
We'll need their artifact URL (S3 or HF).
Sam R.: Also call out KV cache persistence: current runtime supports ephemeral KV caching per worker; persistence across restarts requires enabling prefix cache with Redis. If they want hot warmups, set prefix_cache: true and share cache config.
Elena (AE): Pricing question — they asked if quant variant changes price tiers. Short answer?
Marco (Infra): Yes, quant reduces memory footprint so we can fit 1.5x more concurrent contexts on the same GPU; recommend a 15% discount off standard per-token for q4_k variants for committed capacity POC only. Needs approval from pricing.
Elena (AE): I'll flag to pricing team. Any enterprise blockers left?
Owen (Security): Additions: KMS integration mandatory for Private deploy; SLA language: must include model provenance clause. Also ask them to fill our "model-supply-chain" questionnaire — I've attached the checklist link in the thread (see infrabot).
InfraBot: model-supply-chain checklist created: https://intranet.redwood/models/checklist/PRD-44321 — assigned to Peridot contact.
Anya (Solutions): Action items: 1) Ask customer for model artifact link + SHA, 2) confirm whether custom variant allowed to be uploaded to our catalog or kept in their S3, 3) provide recommended quant/profile matrix + perf targets, 4) pricing approval for q4_k discount.
Sam R.: I'll draft compatibility manifest template and a short client-facing note on recommended runtime flags (batching, prefix_cache, kv_persistence). Draft snippet below: 
```
compatibility_manifest:
  model_id: peridot/llama30b-custom
  supported_quant: [q8_0, q4_k_mixed]
  supported_kernels: [fused_attention_v2, fused_mlp]
  min_gpu_mem_gb: 24
  recommended_batch: 4
  prefix_cache: redis://10.0.0.5:6379
```
Elena (AE): Perfect. I'll ping Peridot to get artifacts and legal answers. ETA for internal deliverables?
Marco (Infra): Perf re-run and infra config by EOD tomorrow. Sam — can you have the manifest draft by noon?
Sam R.: Yep, noon tomorrow.
Owen (Security): I'll review the questionnaire answers within 48 hours of receipt.
Elena (AE): Great — thanks all. I'll update thread when Peridot replies. :thumbsup:
